title: The Electric Face & Two-Headed Worms: Michael Levin's Bioelectric Patterning vs. Canonical Ion-Channel & Morphogen Genetics — From Elmer Lund's 1947 regenerative currents and Oviedo & Levin's permanent two-headed planaria to Adams's optogenetic 'electric face' in Andersen–Tawil Syndrome, Dahal & Bates's Drosophila Irk2–Dpp/BMP secretion proof, Harris's zebrafish kcnk5b fin-scaling critique, and two worked calculations on GHK depolarization, electrotonic cable reach, the 19-fold Ca_v gating paradox, and multi-lab replication power

teenKit.tldr: DNA is just a parts list, not a 3D blueprint, and living tissues use electrical voltage across cell membranes like biological software to decide where to build heads, faces, and tails.
teenKit.whyItMatters: Cracking this bioelectric code could one day allow doctors to rewrite the electrical signals in your body to safely regrow lost limbs or heal severe birth defects.
keyTakeaways: If you chop a flatworm into three pieces, the middle chunk uses localized electrical voltage differences to figure out which cut edge should grow a brain and which should grow a tail.
Briefly blocking cell-to-cell gap junctions can trick flatworms into permanently regenerating two heads from identical DNA, proving memory of body shape exists outside the genome.
Scientists are locked in a fiery debate over whether voltage is an independent software code or just a downstream messenger controlled by traditional molecular genetics.

vocab.meaning: The deep biological mystery of how identical cells with the exact same DNA know what complex 3D shape they are supposed to build or repair.
The electrical voltage difference maintained across a cell's outer membrane, acting like a tiny biological battery.
A chemical substance that flows through developing tissues to help cells determine their position and fate.
A cutting-edge technique that uses pulses of light to control the electrical activity of specific living cells.

quiz.question: If you cut a freshwater flatworm into three pieces, what happens to the middle trunk piece?
options: It dies because the DNA is scrambled
It grows a head on the front and a tail on the back
It turns into a random ball of unorganized cells
quiz.explanation: Even though both cut edges share identical DNA, the trunk successfully builds a brand-new head at the front and a tail at the back.

quiz.question: How do scientists describe the relationship between DNA and an organism's 3D anatomy in this debate?
options: DNA is the 3D software program running the body
DNA is a parts list, while bioelectric patterns act as the software
DNA only dictates hair and eye color, not structure
DNA has no role whatsoever in shaping an organism
quiz.explanation: DNA provides the structural proteins like a parts list, whereas bioelectric patterns act as the software that dictates where those parts go.

quiz.question: What happens when researchers briefly block gap junctions in certain flatworm regeneration experiments?
options: The worm permanently regenerates two heads
The worm doubles in size overnight
quiz.explanation: Temporary gap junction blocks permanently rewrite the anatomical memory of the worm, causing it to grow a second head instead of a tail.
